newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Activists riot in Taipei after nuclear vote.
newsitem.headline: Activists riot in Taipei after nuclear vote.

text.p: Anti-nuclear rioters hurled petrol bombs and rocks and smashed through police barricades on Friday after parliament voted to restore funding for Taiwan's controversial fourth nuclear power station.
As fires burned in the streets outside parliament, police responded by dousing demonstrators with water cannons in one of the worst outbreaks of political chaos to mar Taiwan's fledgling democracy.
The reaction to the controversial late-evening parliamentary vote and the ensuing street violence were broadcast on live television.
A force of 4,000 police with batons and riot shields formed lines outside the parliament building, showing restraint as they held most of the demonstrators at bay.
The violence erupted after Taiwan's deeply divided parliament voted to overturn its May cancellation of its budget for a US$4.1 billion nuclear power station.
The vote itself was delayed for hours by an opposition attempt to filibuster the debate that deteriorated into shoving matches and fistfights inside parliament.
